title: Soviet Transpositions in German, 1919-1920: seven courier letters from communists in Germany to Soviet officials in Russia, seized in Latvia in April 1920 (NARA M336 roll 75)

steps.what: Letter frequencies: German profile in all seven parts (E high, or R high where the copy types R for E); no adjacent-letter dependence, so a transposition.
Simulated annealing over column orders, German 4-gram score: Fortsetzung 4 and Schlussmitteilungen (indicator 27001) give the 19-column key.
Same solver on Zusatz (27003, 940 letters): the 25-column key; it also decrypts Fortsetzung 2 and 5.
Fortsetzung 3 with the 27001 key once the three groups missing from the copy are located; Anfang once a struck-out group (five letters) is removed.
Corrected plaintext re-enciphered and compared letter by letter with the typed copy; every difference checked on the NARA image.
Readings compared with the contemporary English translation (frames 0468-0470) for Anfang, Fortsetzung 3, 4, 5 and Schlussmitteilungen.
cyphersolver catalogue and repository searched (M336 roll 75, Riga, Latvia, indicators, names): nothing on these letters.

validation.notes: Transposition: no substitution key whose values could be scored against a shuffled key; the German 4-gram score that found the keys and the German sentences of the readings are the evidence

outcome.method_basis: Both keys were recovered by a column-order solver scored on German 4-grams, without plaintext; the contemporary English translation in the same file was used afterwards to check the readings.
outcome.fraction_read_source: about 34 of 3,065 plaintext letters left unread (opening and three names of Fortsetzung 2, one letter of a name in Zusatz).

credits.note: keys recovered, seven parts deciphered, transcription checked against the NARA images
State Department English translations of five parts, 1920 (frames 0456, 0468-0470)

gaps.item: Fortsetzung 2: the opening (GALIEIE), OE after 'verdächtig', the names PEL...ZIERSKI and RELCW, and VILARDOVRRHAFEET before 'jetzt frei' (about 34 letters)
gaps.detail: the letters decrypt but do not yet read; no contemporary translation of this part

gaps.item: Zusatz: one letter of the name O?galski
Fortsetzung 3: three groups (15 letters) missing from the typed copy
gaps.detail: letters supplied from the sense and the contemporary translation

texts.label: Seven courier letters, December 1919 - February 1920

reading_review.note: The German of all seven parts was read as sentences. The keys were recovered ciphertext-only from a preliminary, noisy transcription of the blurred copy; each decryption was then edited and corrected, re-enciphered, and the resulting ciphertext checked by eye against the images and found plausible. Remaining holes are the few letters listed under gaps (mainly in Fortsetzung 2).

texts.summary: Reports of the communist secretariat in Germany to Moscow: couriers, money and jewels, addresses, the Vienna branch, the planned congress, the failed Holland conference and arrests, and requests for Radek or Bukharin.

prior.where: The State Department read the letters in 1920: its instruction No. 16 to Riga (5 Aug 1920, frame 0456) encloses translations 'from the code', and a memorandum (frames 0468-0470) gives English translations of five of the seven parts. No German plaintext or key is in the file, and none was found in print.

human: George Lasry set the task and the rules, and directed the image checks; AI language-model agents ran the solvers, read the images and drafted the readings.
